modules.description: Python is the go-to scripting language for penetration testers and the engine behind countless security tools used in the wild, and this module takes you from zero to writing your own. You’ll start with a guided demo to get a feel for the language, move into core programming concepts (variables, control flow, functions, data structures), and build your first standalone scripts. The module finishes with scripts tailored to real pentesting work, so the language becomes a tool you can actually reach for on an engagement.
modules.summary: Pick up Python from the ground up and use it to build practical scripts that power real penetration testing work.

modules.title: Recent Threats
modules.description: Critical vulnerabilities, such as log4j and spring4shell, have taken the world by storm, and it's essential to understand how to exploit them and, even more importantly, the mitigation techniques. This module groups the latest threat labs available on TryHackMe.
modules.summary: Learn about the latest industry threats. Get hands-on experience identifying, exploiting, and mitigating critical vulnerabilities.

modules.title: Red Team Fundamentals
modules.description: This module will introduce the core components and structure of a red team engagement. You will learn how to apply threat intelligence to red team engagements, utilize operations security processes, and set up your own command and control server. By the end of the module, you will be able to plan a red team engagement and understand the methodologies used to emulate a real threat actor.
modules.summary: Learn the core components of a red team engagement, from threat intelligence to OPSEC and C2s.

modules.title: Scripting for Pentesters
modules.description: This module covers the basic usage of the most powerful scripting languages any penetration tester can use; PowerShell and Python. We will explore the basic uses and move towards penetration testing specific tasks. From discovery to network scanning, from keyloggers to post-exploitation scripts, this module covers relevant real-life scenarios that will take your penetration testing craft to the next level. Stop being limited with available tools, build your own.
modules.summary: Learn to use PowerShell and Python in different stages of a penetration test and take your pentesting craft to the next level.

modules.title: Secure AI Systems
modules.description: This module explores AI systems as an attack surface, covering secure architectural design principles and how to identify weaknesses at the system integration layer. Learners examine LLM-specific security concerns, apply threat modelling frameworks like STRIDE and OWASP in AI contexts, and practice attack surface discovery when AI components are present. The module concludes with a static site exercise where learners put their AI threat modelling skills to the test.
modules.summary: Understand how AI systems are architected and how to assess their security posture.

modules.title: Secure Software Development
modules.description: In this module, we learn about DevSecOps, a philosophy that emphasizes integrating security practices throughout the entire software development lifecycle. It explores the benefits and key principles of DevSecOps, highlighting its role in fostering collaboration and enabling the early identification and remediation of vulnerabilities. Next, learners delve into the broader context of DevOps, which emphasizes collaboration and communication between software developers and operations teams. The module highlights the importance of DevOps in enabling rapid and efficient software development and deployment, setting the stage for understanding the interplay between DevOps and Security (DevSecOps).
modules.summary: This module introduces DevSecOps, DevOps, and SDLC. Learn to integrate security into software development for enhanced protection.

modules.title: Securing Compute
modules.description: Every running workload in AWS is a potential target. Exposed management interfaces, unpatched software, abused metadata services, and misconfigured containers are real threats that defenders encounter in production environments. This module takes you through hands-on scenarios built around common attack patterns, teaching you to harden your compute resources.
modules.summary: Compute resources are a prime target in the cloud. From exposed ports to container misconfigurations, learn to recognize and remediate the threats targeting AWS workloads.

modules.title: Security in the Pipeline
modules.description: Unlike the broader focus of the 'Security of the Pipeline' module, which encompasses platform security and tooling, 'Security in the Pipeline' concentrates on ensuring the security of the code as it progresses through the development, testing, and deployment phases. You will gain practical knowledge of implementing SAST and DAST techniques to identify and remediate vulnerabilities early in the development process and test your knowledge with code analysis challenges. Finally, explore the crucial role of dependency management in maintaining a secure pipeline, by learning how to effectively manage and validate dependencies, preventing the introduction of vulnerable or malicious code into the software supply chain. By completing this module, you will acquire essential skills in securing the code flow, thus bolstering the overall resilience and integrity of the DevSecOps pipeline.
modules.summary: Security in the Pipeline module focuses on securing the code, encompassing SAST, DAST, code analysis challenges, and dependency management for robust DevSecOps practices.

modules.title: Security Information and Event Management
modules.description: This module explores SIEM basics - how logs are ingested and searched over to get the answers and how to identify the anomalies. This module also covers features standard in each SIEM solution, such as timeline, search bar, time filter and how to construct search queries to find anomalous traces. Aspiring security analysts can quickly transfer the knowledge covered in this module into any SIEM solution.
modules.summary: Understand how SIEM works and get comfortable creating simple and advanced search queries to look for specific answers from the ingested logs.

modules.title: Security of the Pipeline
modules.description: The 'Security of the Pipeline' module is the second milestone in the DevSecOps pathway. This module explores the comprehensive security considerations required to safeguard the journey of code throughout the software development lifecycle. By understanding the intricacies of code flow and implementing appropriate security measures at each step, learners gain valuable insights into maintaining a secure and robust software development pipeline. You will learn about pipelines in a secure and automated way, experiment with CI/CD security as part of platform security. Learn how to keep source code secure, understand code versioning and gain insights into securing the build process to prevent tampering and unauthorized changes.
modules.summary: This module focuses on platform security, tooling, and the secure flow of code. Explore broader aspects of securing the code's journey through the development, testing, and deployment phases.

modules.title: Security Operations & Monitoring
modules.description: Defenders use a variety of tools that make up the security stack such as Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) and Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR) tools. Defenders need to know how to configure these tools properly and utilise them to gain visibility and identify anomalous activity in their network. This module will explore these different tools used to monitor and detect threats on the network and endpoints.
modules.summary: Learn how to configure and utilise tooling to ensure that suspicious activity is quickly identified and dealt within your environment.

modules.title: Security Solutions
modules.description: In this module, you will learn how essential defensive security solutions work, such as firewalls, Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS), vulnerability scanners, and Security Information and Event Management (SIEM). Through hands-on exercises, you will learn how to use firewalls to allow or block traffic, IDS to detect intrusions, vulnerability scanners to find vulnerabilities, and the SIEM solution to monitor centralized security events. This module will equip you with the arsenal to protect digital infrastructure.
modules.summary: Explore fundamental defensive security solutions like firewalls, IDS, vulnerability scanners, and SIEM through different hands-on exercises.

modules.title: Shells and Privilege Escalation
modules.description: Having limited user access on a system won't give you the necessary privileges you need to fully exploit it. Privilege escalation is an essential part of any security engagement. This module will give you the necessary skills to enumerate and identify how a system can be made vulnerable. You'll get hands on by fully exploiting a variety of machines, through various vulnerabilities and misconfigurations; kernel exploits, vulnerable services and permission issues are a few of the techniques you'll use to gain system level access.
modules.summary: Once you have initial access on a machine, learn how to escalate your account privileges to root.

modules.title: SIEM Triage for SOC
modules.description: In this module, you will learn to apply a systematic approach to SIEM investigations: where to focus your attention, and which queries to run to get the answers quickly. You will investigate various scenarios in Splunk and Elastic across web, Linux, and Windows environments, sharpening the triage skills, which every SOC analyst needs to succeed.
modules.summary: Explore how SIEM solutions help detect early signs of attacks, investigate SOC alerts, and correlate logs to build an incident timeline.

modules.title: Snort
modules.description: This module will cover the need-to-know functionalities of Snort for any security analyst: Traffic Sniffing, Traffic Logging, Traffic Blocking, PCAP investigation, and creating IDS/IPS rules. You will learn how to use Snort for different purposes and create IDS/IPS rules for different threat scenarios. By the End of the module, you will master your Snort skills and be able to detect anomalies and threats and stop malicious activities.
modules.summary: Snort is the most widely used Open Source Intrusion Detection & Prevention System and is essential in defining malicious network activity.

modules.title: Snyk
modules.description: This module introduces the fundamentals of using Snyk to enhance software security. You will learn to identify and understand security risks in open-source dependencies and codebases, effectively detect vulnerabilities, and apply remediation measures. The module also covers integrating security testing throughout the software development lifecycle and measuring the impact of security tools to ensure a robust security posture for your projects.
modules.summary: Secure your code and dependencies. Learn to detect, evaluate, and remediate vulnerabilities with Snyk.

modules.title: SOC Level 1 Capstone Challenges
modules.description: In this module, you will handle real-world incidents composed of different Tactics, Techniques, and Procedures (TTPs), starting from initial access to data exfiltration. You will learn how to handle different artefacts, including memory dumps, email samples, packet captures, and event logs. Additionally, you will learn how to navigate different data sources ingested in an SIEM and correlate the significant findings to complete the investigation.
modules.summary: Investigate critical incidents and apply all the skills needed to be an effective SOC analyst while handling various artefacts.

modules.title: SOC Level 2 Capstone Challenges
modules.description: In this module, you will work with Splunk and Elastic to investigate breaches based on real-world incidents. You will also complete one on-host Linux analysis challenge and one threat intelligence challenge, covering the different duties an L2 analyst can have. Once finished, you should be well-prepared for the SAL2 certification. Good luck!
modules.summary: Practice what you’ve learned throughout the SOC Level 2 learning path in a series of log analysis, threat hunting, and threat intelligence challenges.

modules.title: SOC Team Internals
modules.description: This module is built around the central concept of any SOC team - security alerts. You will learn to triage and classify alerts, document findings, write reports, and follow proper escalation and communication procedures. These skills will help you build confidence for TryHackMe SOC-SIM and your first months in a real SOC team.
modules.summary: Explore the essential SOC analyst skills to help you triage, classify, and escalate alerts in real-world SOC environments.

modules.title: Software Basics
modules.description: This module introduces the core building blocks behind software: data representation and encoding. You’ll learn how computers store colours, numbers, and text, and how character encoding turns letters into numeric values that systems can understand. After that, you’ll get hands-on demos in Python and JavaScript, building familiarity with key programming concepts. You’ll finish by exploring databases and learning how SQL is used to retrieve and manage stored data.
modules.summary: Explore how computers handle data behind the scenes, and try your first steps in Python, JavaScript, and SQL.

modules.title: Software Security
modules.description: This module will introduce you to the software development lifecycle and the core security controls that can be integrated into it to prevent vulnerabilities in the final product. You’ll learn about the most common vulnerabilities in web applications and APIs, and how to integrate DAST and SAST tools into early development phases to detect and mitigate them proactively.
modules.summary: Understand how security integrates into the development process of an application, and learn how to mitigate common vulnerabilities in web applications.

modules.title: Specialized Domains
modules.description: This module branches out beyond the core pentesting path into the specialized domains shaping modern cyber security. You’ll explore wireless, mobile, and cloud security to see how each environment introduces its own attack surface, step into the rapidly emerging world of LLM pentesting, and shift perspective to see how defenders tackle the same problems through the blue team lens and DevSecOps practices. By the end, you’ll have a clear picture of where the field is going and which specialization might be right for you.
modules.summary: Branch out into specialized cyber security domains, from wireless and mobile security to cloud, LLM pentesting, defense, and DevSecOps.

modules.title: Start Your Cyber Security Journey
modules.description: This module introduces the reader to offensive cyber security through an interactive exercise where users can practice hacking an insecure web application in a legal and safe environment. Then, it presents defensive security via an interactive exercise to protect against an attack. Finally, it equips the reader with the fundamental search skills to find what they need as they start their journey in cyber security.
modules.summary: Explore offensive and defensive cyber security via interactive exercises and acquire the essential search skills to find information.

modules.title: Starters
modules.description: This module offers a collection of fun, standalone CTF-style challenges designed to help learners build practical hacking skills. These are not part of a linear learning path but serve as valuable, varied practice for foundational techniques across different domains.
modules.summary: A collection of fun independent challenges that should not be overlooked.

modules.title: Static Malware Analysis
modules.description: In this module, we will learn how to understand a malware's purpose and behavior just by looking at its metadata, properties, and actual code. We will explore the tools used to analyse binaries, scripts, and MS Office files, and practice on real-world malware examples.
modules.summary: Learn how to perform static malware analysis by investigating malware binaries, scripts, and MS Office documents without running them in sandbox.

modules.title: Storage and Data Security
modules.description: Storage misconfigurations are among the most common causes of cloud data breaches and among the most preventable. From publicly accessible objects to snapshots shared beyond their intended audience, the risks are significant and the impact severe. This module explores how AWS storage services can be inadvertently exposed, teaches you how to spot them, and equips you with the controls needed to keep your data secure.
modules.summary: Data breaches often begin with a misconfigured bucket or an exposed snapshot. Learn to secure AWS storage and prevent sensitive data from reaching the wrong hands.

modules.title: Threat Analysis Tools
modules.description: This module explores the foundations of threat intelligence, covering data sources, enrichment and analytical methods. You will work with files, hashes, IPs, domains, and intelligence feeds to identify threats, track adversary behaviour, and connect findings to MITRE ATT&CK techniques. By the end, you will know how to operationalise threat intelligence in investigations and reporting.
modules.summary: Gain practical skills in using threat intelligence, enrichment tools, and analysis workflows to strengthen your SOC capabilities.

modules.title: Threat and Vulnerability Management
modules.description: As defenders, the objective is to stop an adversary from achieving their goal. These adversaries are using both their own trade craft and other methods to launch attacks against organisations. This module will explore the various tools and methodologies that will help defenders keep up with the latest threat intelligence to understand how adversaries are operating and apply it to your defense strategy.
modules.summary: Identify how attackers are developing their techniques to use in your defensive strategy.

modules.title: Threat Emulation
modules.description: In this module, we’ll showcase the benefits of understanding different threat actors' Tactics, Techniques, and Procedures through adversary emulation and learn to defend against them by seeing them in action. You will learn how to plan threat emulation activities through different Threat Modeling frameworks and execute them through Atomic Red Team and Caldera. Additionally, you’ll be observing these emulation activities from a defender's perspective.
modules.summary: Understand the core concepts of threat emulation and learn how to execute adversarial activity through different threat emulation frameworks.

modules.title: Threat Emulation
modules.description: Emulation is the act of imitating or mimicking a person. Defenders can imitate, or emulate, an adversarial threat against the security stack in place. With this process, defenders can measure the security stack's effectiveness and close any gaps in coverage.
modules.summary: The best way to understand how attackers work is to get hands-on experience with their techniques.

modules.title: Threat Hunting
modules.description: In this module, we’ll tackle ways to hunt known Tactics, Techniques and Procedures (TTPs) using different methodologies of threat hunting. You will learn to effectively differentiate benign and malicious activity from a large dataset of logs ingested in a SIEM. Additionally, you will be tasked to hunt and investigate scenarios that typically occur in real life.
modules.summary: Understand the fundamentals of threat hunting, and learn how to build your own methodology for effective hunting across your infrastructure.

modules.title: Threat Hunting
modules.description: In this module, you will progress through threat hunting from fundamentals to hands-on investigation. Starting with core concepts and methodologies, you will learn to hunt known tactics and techniques using real data in a SIEM. The module builds progressively. Each room covers a different phase of an attack chain, from initial access through impact. By the end, you will have conducted threat hunts end-to-end and investigated real-world scenarios, preparing you to hunt threats proactively in your own infrastructure.
modules.summary: Learn threat hunting fundamentals and investigate real attack scenarios to find threats across your infrastructure.

modules.title: Threats and Risks
modules.description: In this module, we will be exploring the concepts of threat and risk management. Security engineers often have to help identify and classify potential threats. This helps to better understand security issues before they can fully become vulnerabilities. Similarly, risk management is required to decide what will be best to help mitigate the risk. The answer isn’t always just to deploy more security, as security has a cost. In this module, we will look to better understand that a balance approach to security is required.
modules.summary: Understand how security engineers help their organisations to identify threats and risks to better manage them.

modules.title: Tools and Code Analysis
modules.description: This module starts by introducing Metasploit to help you exploit system vulnerabilities. It demonstrates using Wireshark to inspect network traffic and Burp Suite to intercept web traffic exchanged with web servers and applications. For brute-forcing various login systems, Hydra is presented. The module concludes with introducing Python for penetration testers.
modules.summary: Explore penetration testing tools like Metasploit, Wireshark, and Burp Suite. Furthermore, discover using Python for penetration testing.

modules.title: TryHack3M Special
modules.description: Celebrate 3 million users with us! The TryHackMe Team has prepared a unique series of 3-million-themed challenges to test your skills. The challenges cover a wide range of topics, including: Exploiting chained vulnerabilities, Supply chain attacks, Reverse engineering of custom cryptography, Smart contracts hacking, SQL injection, Threat hunting, and Code analysis
modules.summary: Celebrate 3 Million Users with TryHackMe by solving five 3-million-themed challenges. Topics range from supply chain attacks to threat hunting!

modules.title: Vulnerability Knowledge
modules.description: This module is about how penetration testers stay ahead of the curve, starting with the public vulnerability databases (CVE, NVD, vendor advisories) that catalog every known weakness in modern software. You’ll then move into the scanning tools that do the heavy lifting at scale, before picking up the manual identification techniques that turn raw scanner output into reliable, actionable findings. By the end, you’ll know how to research a CVE from first principles and validate whether it actually applies to a target.
modules.summary: Learn how to research vulnerabilities in public databases, scan for them with industry tools, and identify them in real systems.

modules.title: Vulnerability Research
modules.description: In this module, you will learn about various categories of vulnerabilities, how they can be scored by severity, and how to effectively research them to find publicly written exploits. Each room in this module will require you to find and exploit different vulnerabilities, both manually and through automation.
modules.summary: Familiarise yourself with the skills, research methods, and resources used to exploit vulnerable applications and systems.

modules.title: Wazuh for SOC and GRC
modules.description: Learn how to leverage Wazuh to satisfy both SOC and GRC requirements. Explore Wazuh's core architecture, vulnerability detection, and compliance reporting before diving into detection engineering with custom alert rules and decoders. To complement Wazuh, the module introduces Osquery for deep system visibility during threat hunting.
modules.summary: This module teaches analysts how to use Wazuh and Osquery for continuous endpoint monitoring, custom threat detection, and compliance auditing.

modules.title: Web Application Security Fundamentals
modules.description: This module opens your web application testing journey by teaching you to walk through a target the way an attacker does, surfacing the hidden pages, directories, and files that ordinary users never see. You’ll then dig into the modern stacks that power today’s sites, understanding how frontend frameworks, APIs, and backend technologies each introduce their own attack surface. By the end, you’ll be running practical web server attacks and reading them through a pentester’s lens.
modules.summary: Map how modern web applications are built, uncover their hidden endpoints, and exploit the most common web server weaknesses.

modules.title: Web Application Vulnerabilities I
modules.description: This module walks you through five of the most impactful vulnerabilities in modern web applications, examining how each works, why it persists, and how attackers exploit it in the wild. You’ll start with the classics, SQL injection and cross-site scripting, before moving to subtler bugs like CSRF, SSRF, and IDOR that often slip past even experienced developers. A final hands-on challenge brings all the techniques together, so you finish the module able to spot these issues quickly and exploit them with confidence.
modules.summary: Exploit five of the most impactful web vulnerabilities, from SQL injection to IDOR, and prove your skills in a hands-on challenge.

modules.title: Web Application Vulnerabilities II
modules.description: This module takes your web hacking beyond the classics into the vulnerabilities that turn small oversights into full-system compromises. You’ll begin with the mechanics of session management and authentication, then move on to server-side attacks such as directory traversal and command injection, and finish with the rapidly expanding attack surface of modern APIs. A live security challenge closes the module, so the techniques are battle-tested before you carry them into the rest of the path.
modules.summary: Tackle deeper web vulnerabilities like broken authentication, command injection, and API flaws, then prove yourself in a live challenge.

modules.title: Web Frameworks
modules.description: This module covers white-box web application testing: tracing a vulnerability from source code to a working exploit across the frameworks that carry most production traffic. Learners start with the review method itself, reading code, mapping attack surface, and grepping for dangerous patterns, before applying it stack by stack. Spring Boot brings Actuator misconfiguration, SQL injection below the ORM, mass assignment, and deserialisation. Django and Flask bring debug exposure, session forgery, and template injection. ASP.NET brings ViewState tampering, mass assignment, and deserialisation. Each framework room ends with a practical task chaining that stack's bugs into one exploit path, and a hard capstone challenge closes the module by combining four Spring Boot flaws in a single unredacted codebase to reach remote code execution.
modules.summary: Learn how to read a framework's source code like an attacker and exploit the bugs it ships by default.

modules.title: Web Hacking
modules.description: This module helps the user become familiar with web applications, JavaScript, database systems, and SQL. Furthermore, it teaches the basics of BurpSuite so the user gains the necessary knowledge to conduct various web application security tests.
modules.summary: Learn about web applications, JavaScript, SQL and explore BurpSuite, a web application security testing platform.

modules.title: Web Hacking Fundamentals
modules.description: In this module, we'll be exploring the basic components of the modern web including both the basic protocols used, as well as various server components that make up the world wide web. You'll be diving into how to use BurpSuite, a tool which is widely regarded to be at the heart of web hacking. Additionally, you'll learn how to perform basic enumeration of websites and exploit the ten most common web application vulnerabilities by hacking various real-world applications.
modules.summary: Understand the core security issues with web applications, and learn how to exploit them using industry tools and techniques.

modules.title: Web Security Monitoring
modules.description: In this module, you will learn how the web works and how modern web threats can affect both end users and application owners. You will use network captures, raw logs, and SIEM to understand how different web attacks unfold and how to detect them in a SOC. Beyond the logs, you will explore not just how to detect threats but also how to stop them with tools like WAF and CDN.
modules.summary: Learn how to protect and monitor the web, the ecosystem every organisation relies upon to deliver its services, all in a series of SOC-oriented labs and real-world scenarios.

modules.title: Welcome to AWS
modules.description: AWS is one of the largest cloud providers, and understanding how it works is the first step to securing it. This module introduces you to the building blocks of AWS: how identities are created and managed, how networks are structured, how data is stored, and what tools AWS provides to defend it all. Whether you are new to cloud or coming from a different background, this module sets the stage for everything that follows.
modules.summary: Cloud security starts with understanding the platform. Build a solid foundation across AWS core services, identity, networking, storage, and native security tooling.

modules.title: WindCorp
modules.description: We try to make these boxes as life-like as possible, based on our own experiences, frustrations and amazements. Most of the things you encounter, we have encountered as well, or we have found a shiny new exploit that we have tried out and like to share with you.
modules.summary: Hack your way through WindCorp in this themed module of hands-on challenges that simulate real-world attacks across a fictional company's infrastructure.

modules.title: Windows and AD Fundamentals
modules.description: Keep existing description: Windows is the most popular operating system, used by individuals and corporate environments worldwide. This module will help you become comfortable using essential Windows features (in a safe environment), including user account permissions, resource management and monitoring, registry access, and security controls. It will also introduce you to Active Directory (AD) basics.
modules.summary: Get hands-on access to Windows and it's security controls. These basics will help you in identifying, exploiting and defending Windows.

modules.title: Windows Endpoint Investigation
modules.description: In this module, we will explore various aspects of Windows Forensics and how different components within Windows store information about the user activity and system configuration that could help us during a digital investigation. You will learn about file systems, registry changes, and network activity generated from user activity. At the end of this module, you will be comfortable performing digital forensics on Windows Endpoints.
modules.summary: Understand various aspects of Windows forensics and learn how to investigate the footprints of an attack on the Windows Endpoint.

modules.title: Windows Exploitation Basics
modules.description: Windows is the most popular operating system, used by both individuals and within corporate environments. Windows systems are often linked together to create networks, which are used in most enterprises around the world. This module will explore everything from getting started with using Windows, to attacking common flaws that are found in common Windows systems.
modules.summary: Hacking Windows is often daunting. Grasp the fundamentals of core Windows concepts and Active Directory vulnerabilities.

modules.title: Windows Fundamentals
modules.description: Windows is the most popular operating system, used by both individuals and corporate environments all around the world. This module will get you comfortable using some of the key Windows features (in a safe environment), including user account permissions, resource management and monitoring, registry access and security controls.
modules.summary: Get hands-on access to Windows and it's security controls. These basics will help you in identifying, exploiting and defending Windows.
keyLearnings: Understand Windows UI, file system, and core features.
Manage users, permissions, and security controls.
Configure settings and monitor resources with built-ins.
Work with the Registry to manage configurations.
Use built-in security features to protect systems.

modules.title: Windows Security Monitoring
modules.description: This module explores the Windows attacks and defenses directly on the host, without SIEM abstractions. You will use Event Viewer, the command line, and file system navigation to detect real malware samples and learn the corresponding MITRE techniques. This hands-on experience will sharpen your Windows skills and prepare you for real-world SOC work.
modules.summary: Learn how Windows logging works and how you can use it to detect common Windows attacks - all through real-world examples and challenging, hands-on threat detection labs.

modules.title: Wireshark
modules.description: This module will cover need-to-know functionalities of Wireshark for any security analyst: Traffic Sniffing, Packet Dissection & Navigation, Packet Filtering, and Traffic Analysis. You will learn how to use Wireshark when investigating live and captured traffic and identify anomalies, threats and attacks. By the end of the module, you will master your Wireshark skills and be able to investigate complex network cases and create IOC lists and actionable results with Wireshark.
modules.summary: Wireshark is the industry-standard tool for network protocol analysis and is essential in any kind of traffic investigation.

modules.title: Wonderland
modules.description: This module is designed to test your CTF problem-solving skills. It presents fictional, themed challenges inspired by Alice in Wonderland and offers limited guidance. It’s perfect for learners ready to apply what they know.
modules.summary: Designed to test your enumeration, privilege escalation, and CTF skills. Will you get lost in Wonderland, or manage to leave with the flags?
